pr_title: fix(rust, python): raise if tz_localize called on UTC-aware

issue_context.title: tz_localize is allowed (but ignored?) when current timezone is UTC?
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://crates.io/crates/polars) of Polars.


### Issue description

Calling `tz_localize` on a tz-aware Series errors. Unless it's UTC, in which case the call is just ignored?

### Reproducible example

```
In [2]: ts_utc = pl.Series(['2018-10-28']).str.strptime(pl.Datetime).dt.tz_localize('UTC')

In [3]: ts_utc
Out[3]:
shape: (1,)
Series: '' [datetime[μs, UTC]]
[
        2018-10-28 00:00:00 UTC
]

In [4]: ts_utc.dt.tz_localize('US/Pacific')
Out[4]:
shape: (1,)
Series: '' [datetime[μs, UTC]]
[
        2018-10-28 00:00:00 UTC
]
```

### Expected behavior

I think I'd expect
```
ComputeError: Cannot localize a tz-aware datetime. Consider using 'dt.with_time_zone' or 'dt.cast_time_zone'
```

Either that, or to set the new timezone. Probably the former (error).
